        Welcome to the Week 7 grades!We have somehow hit the final Sunday of October, and when you look at the NFL standings, there are definitely a few surprises. For one, the Cleveland Browns are in first place in their division. I repeat, the Cleveland Browns are in first place. This is not a drill. One reason the Browns' magical run is happening is because of Deshaun Watson. During Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee, Watson engineered another fourth-quarter game-winning drive on Sunday, and he now has five on the season. That makes him just the third QB since 1970 to have a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season. Not to be outdone, the New York Giants are also in first place of the NFC East, AND they just won a game with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback. If I had told you in August that the first-place Giants were going to win a Week 7 game with J.J. McCarthy under center, I would have been laughed at on the internet. No one's laughing now. The Giants have now won a game with three different starting quarterbacks this year (McCarthy, Jameis Winston and Jaxson Dart). That makes them the first team since the 2016 Patriots to win at least three games with three different starters before November. On the other side of the standings, the Baltimore Ravens are in last place after suffering one of the most shocking losses in NFL history. The Ravens led the Bengals 13-0 at halftime but ultimately lost 35-13. That's the third-largest loss in NFL history by a team that led by at least 13 points at halftime. Since 2020, the Ravens have lost 17 games in which they led by double digits at some point, the most in the NFL in that span. All three of their losses this year have come in games where they held a double-digit lead. This was the second straight week where they shut out their opponent in the first half, only to go scoreless and lose in the second half. To make matters worse for the Ravens, the two teams we mentioned earlier -- the Giants and Browns -- are coached by two people the Ravens got rid of at the end of last season (John Harbaugh and Todd Monken). 
Speaking of Harbaugh, Dallas is now just one game behind his Giants in the NFC East after beating the Eagles on Monday night. With that in mind, let's get to the grades, starting with the Cowboys big win. Cowboys (3-4) 38-21 over Eagles (2-5)Bengals (4-2) 35-13 over Ravens (4-3)Seahawks (3-4) 20-3 over Chiefs (5-1)Lions (4-2) 20-17 over Packers (4-3)Rams (3-4) 35-21 over Raiders (3-4)Broncos (5-2) 30-16 over Cardinals (2-5)Falcons (3-4) 29-20 over 49ers (6-1)Vikings (6-0) 16-10 over Colts (2-5)Giants (4-2-1) 27-21 over Texans (2-5)Buccaneers (2-5) 43-13 Panthers (3-3)Browns (5-2) 27-24 over Titans (1-6)Dolphins (1-5) 28-25 over Jets (2-5)Steelers (5-2) 16-10 over Saints (2-5) in ParisBears (5-2) 30-24 over Patriots (4-3)

title: Oregon QB Dante Moore won't return in 2026 after concussion, Dan Lanning confirms - CBS Sports
description: Moore, who turned down the 2026 NFL Draft for a return to Oregon, has not played since suffering the head injury
body:
Moore, who turned down the 2026 NFL Draft for a return to Oregon, has not played since suffering the head injury against USC on Sept. 26
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oregon doesn't expect quarterback Dante Moore to return from his concussion this season, coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday. Moore hasn't played since Sept. 26, when he suffered a head injury after taking a late hit to the head from USC linebacker Desman Stephens II."We really got clarity for us this last week," Lanning said. "If it was up to Dante in any shape or way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. Unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante. It's not really up to me. We can control the setting in practice where he's able to do things for us, but that's not always the case in the game."We said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100 percent be able to make a full recovery from. That hasn't changed. For him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not going to happen."Lanning added that he anticipates Moore playing a role for the Ducks, even though he won't be able to play in game action, including helping the defense improve in practice.
"We're getting one of the best scout team looks every single week in practice, and he looks good out there," Lanning said.Prior to his injury, Moore completed 69.7% of his passes for 926 yards, nine touchdowns and zero interceptions. Last season, when Moore earned third-team All-Big Ten honors, he connected on 71.8% of his passing attempts for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.With Moore out of the lineup, the Oregon offense has been among the worst in Big Ten play as the team has oscillated between backups Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Those shortcomings resulted in the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday.
Asked what he needs to see out of Raiola and Thomas moving forward, Lanning emphasized "consistency," especially when it comes to starting games well."We've been a really good quarterback room off the bench," Lanning said. "We haven't been a very good quarterback room consistently at the start of games."Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) returns to action Saturday against No. 20 Northwestern.
Has Moore played his last game at Oregon?Even after last season, Moore was projected to be a first-round NFL Draft pick, but he chose to return to college in hopes of winning a national championship.Obviously, the season didn't go to plan for Moore or Oregon, and he will have another decision to make at the end of the 2026 campaign. Lanning said he hasn't spoken with Moore about his plans while adding that his focus is on the season at hand."That's not fair for me to say or speculate," Lanning said. "He'll have a decision at the end of the season about what that looks like. I think we all can acknowledge Dante is a great player, and he'll get the opportunity to be drafted.
"What that looks like in the future, that's a decision for a later date. We haven't had that conversation. I don't know where his mind is at. That's not where my focus is, and I don't think that's where his focus is right now."Due to the NCAA's new five-year eligibility policy, Moore could return to Oregon for the 2027 season. Despite the injury, Moore is once again projected to be a first-round pick, although opinions vary on exactly where he could land.On one hand, Moore may not want to risk returning for another season, given the fact that a slow start and a season-ending injury have undoubtedly hurt his draft stock. On the other hand, would Moore have any interest in proving his health and working his way back up draft boards next fall?
Another factor Moore will have to consider when making his decision is the state of the quarterback crop in the 2027 draft class, which isn't getting rave reviews. There's a chance Moore would be one of the more enticing signal callers in the draft if he decides to make that jump.

title: 2026 World Series: Jackson Chourio just showing off as the face of the Brewers - CBS Sports
description: In Game 3 on Monday, Chourio became the youngest player with a four-hit World Series game since Joe Garagiola in
body:
In Game 3 on Monday, Chourio became the youngest player with a four-hit World Series game since Joe Garagiola in 1946
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ST. PETERSBURG -- Game 3 of the World Series was a total bloodbath. The Brewers now have a 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series after a 10-1 drubbing of whatever is left of the Rays. Pick your phrase: men vs. boys, varsity vs. JV. This has been less a series than an inevitability.The Brewers are now 7-0 in the NLCS and World Series. The only team previously to sweep both of the last two rounds was the 1976 Reds, but that Big Red Machine only had a five-game NLCS. The Brewers can make it 8-0 for the first time in MLB history with a win in Game 4.First things first, though. Let's discuss this Game 3 monstrosity from the Crew. They recorded 10 runs on 16 hits, compared to 1 and 3 from the Rays -- and it was worse than it looked because the Rays got a run on two hits in the ninth when it was already basically over. It was domination from start to finish, while the Rays were bumbling and ineffectual. Front and center for the winners? Jackson Chourio, of course. Heading into the series, I noted that Chourio and Rays third baseman Junior Caminero were going to have the national spotlight here in this World Series as up-and-coming superstars. Chourio has been up to the task and then some. He led off the game with a line drive single, then came through with singles in each of his next two at-bats, too. In his fourth at-bat, he doubled during the game-changing, eight-run fifth inning. 
"Yeah, I think that you could say this is one of my better games," Chourio said after the game. "Really, I was just taking every at-bat like it could be my last and trying to find any way I could to get on base. Because I know, as long as I get on base, there's guys behind me who could score."
That fifth-inning double was the weakest of his four hits at 99 mph (95+ are considered "hard hit" balls). Chourio put up four hits, two runs and an RBI through five innings. The Rays as a team recorded zero runs on one hit through eight. Remember, Chourio is still only 22 years old. In Game 3, he became the youngest player with a four-hit World Series game since Joe Garagiola in 1946. It was the first time in 80 years! That's how talented this wunderkind is. 
"Nobody's surprised that Jack Jack's doing this. Nobody's surprised. He's turning into -- 20, 21, 22, he's turning into a fine player. He's understanding what it takes, the discipline that it takes. He's coming into his own. Nobody's shocked. He's just really, really good," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Game 3."He's also played incredible defense, and he stole a base tonight. He's a total player. Like we talked about, you ask about Kobe Bryant and him. Kobe strived to get better and better and better every year because he was so disciplined. He was such a worker. He had such an attitude. Jackson's on that same track."The Brewers churn out talent from all over the spectrum. They get the absolute most out of retreads like Jake Bauers, as well as organizational guys like Game 3 starter Robert Gasser. And then there are superstar prospects like Chourio. 
He won't finish that high in MVP voting this season, but it might be the last time for a long time. Injury held him to 127 games this season and he still posted 4.9 WAR. He's gone 20-20 (home runs and steals) in three seasons already. We've seen all five tools in the playoffs. The hit tool? Yeah, he's 8 for 14 in the World Series, good for a cool .571 average. Power? He's hit two home runs in the postseason so far. Speed? He stole a base in Game 3, giving him three World Series steals so far. The glove and arm were on display in Game 2, when he threw out an all-important Rays baserunner at home. When you watch Chourio play, he makes you feel like there's nothing he can't do on a baseball field. It's true, and he's only starting to scratch the proverbial surface. He wouldn't be a bad prediction for National League MVP next season. But first, he's strutting his stuff on the biggest stage.
Anyone who has watched him play regularly isn't surprised one bit by the performance in this World Series. He's long had the talent and confidence and swagger of a superstar. And just as importantly, he's signed with the Brewers on a team-friendly deal through the 2031 season with two more club options running through 2033. He's poised to be the face of the organization for a long time. The Brewers are better in every facet, and the Rays blew their only opening in three games so far when they put up four runs in the first inning of Game 2, then failed to score again in a 5-4 loss. Hell, they haven't scored since. And they got the doors blown off them in Game 3 by the superior team. In the case of men vs. boys here, one of the youngest players in the series is the biggest, baddest man of all.

title: NFL schedule: League makes rare double flex move by tweaking Week 9 and Week 11 - CBS Sports
description: The NFL just tweaked the schedule for two different weeks in November
body:
The NFL just tweaked the schedule for two different weeks in November
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL rarely announces two weeks' worth of schedule changes at the same time, but that's exactly what the league did Monday. For just the second time this year, the NFL has decided to utilize its flex scheduling powers. This time around, the league is changing the television network for four games while tweaking the kickoff time for one of them. Of the games that were rescheduled, two will kick off in Week 9, while the other two will take place in Week 11. Let's take a look at the changes, starting with the two moves that got made in Week 9. 
WEEK 9 (Nov. 8)Raiders at 49ers, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS)Lions at Dolphins, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on CBS)With this change, the Raiders-49ers game will now be moved into the prime viewing window for Week 9. Fox has the national doubleheader that week, and the network will now have three games to feature in the 4:25 p.m. ET window, with Packers-Patriots and Cardinals-Seahawks also airing on Fox at that time. With 49ers-Raiders moving to Fox, the Texans at Chargers will be the only CBS game in the late window, kicking off at 4:05 p.m. ET. Now, let's check out the changes for Week 11WEEK 11 (Nov. 22)Buccaneers at Lions, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on CBS)Dolphins at Bills, 1 p.m. ET on CBS (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on Fox)The Bills will be moving from Fox to CBS in Week 11, which is certainly the notable news here. Fox actually had a Bills game earlier this season, which is probably one reason this flex went through: the network probably wouldn't have been thrilled to lose that game if it had been its only chance to feature Josh Allen this season. 
With these four flex moves now in the books, there's still one big question to answer in Week 9 and that's whether the NFL ends up flexing the Sunday night game. The Buccaneers are currently scheduled to play in Chicago on Sunday night, but with Tampa Bay sitting at 2-5, the NFL could flex the game. The league has to decide whether to move the kickoff time by the end of the day on Tuesday (Oct. 27). As things currently stand, this is the only Sunday night game on the Bears' schedule, so the NFL might be hesitant to move them out of it. Not to mention, the Bucs have won two of their past three games, so they've certainly looked more competitive over the past few weeks following a 0-4 start. Based on those two facts, it wouldn't be surprising at all if the Buccaneers-Bears end up staying put.

title: Who will Jay-Z bring out for the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show? Four possible guests - CBS Sports
description: Will Jay Z bring out any guests? If he does, here are some guesses of who they could be
body:
Will Jay Z bring out any guests? If he does, here are some guesses of who they could be
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's official: Jay-Z will take the stage for the Super Bowl halftime show on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are partners with the NFL on the halftime show, having produced the event since 2019. The rapper is a key decision-maker in who performs, and this year he chose himself.While we know who the performer will be during the biggest game in American sports, we do not know who will be playing in the Super Bowl. We'll have to wait until the last day of January for that one.Another mystery that remains is who, if anyone, will be his special guest(s). Many halftime show performers bring out additional artists, and while Jay-Z has not announced any yet, there is a good chance he will.Here is a look at artists that he could bring out, based on their past history and collaborations:
BeyonceQueen Bey is first on the list for obvious reasons. The superstar singer has been married to Jay-Z since 2018 and shares three children together.The two have worked together numerous times, including their first collaboration before they were dating, "'03 Bonnie and Clyde." Their most popular song together is arguably "Crazy in Love," released in 2003. Other collaborations include "Drunk in Love," "Part II (On the Run)," "Deja Vu" and "Lift Off." They toured together, so they are used to sharing the same stage. She also has a history of performing on the NFL stage. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime in Houston for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyoncé Bowl."
RihannaJay-Z was pivotal in Rihanna's early success. In 2005, as CEO of Def Jam Records, Jay-Z had Rihanna audition for him and others, and the rest is history. She eventually left Def Jam for Roc Nation in 2010.The two have multiple songs together, including "Umbrella," "Run This Town," and "FourFiveSeconds."Earlier this year, she was a surprise guest at his tour, joining him on stage at Yankee Stadium, a main character in many of Jay-Z's songs.
Rihanna is another potential special guest, who is no stranger to the NFL. She was the Super Bowl headliner in 2023 and had one of the most memorable performances in recent history, announcing her pregnancy during the event. Blu Ivy CarterBlu Ivy Carter is the oldest child of Jay-Z and Beyoncé. She performed as a dancer during Beyonce's 2024 Christmas Day halftime show in Houston. Blu Ivy also joined her mom for the Cowboy Carter tour, once again as a dancer. For being so young, she already has a huge fanbase, with concertgoers holding signs for her, yelling her name at shows and tweeting about her talents.Not only has Ms. Carter performed on an NFL stage before, but she is also often seen attending NFL games with her dad. The Super Bowl halftime show could turn into a family affair.
EminemSlim Shady joined Jay Z on stage during his current tour, and the two could have another reunion at the Super Bowl. The two collaborated on the song "Renegade" on Jay-Z's album The Blueprint.Like the others on the list, Eminem has experience as an NFL performer. His comes via the 2022 Super Bowl, where he was a special guest on an iconic hip-hop lineup.

title: Who's to blame for Manchester United's decline? Ranking the biggest culprits - CBS Sports
description: It's happened again. Another season, another Manchester United crisis. No longer does the end of daylight savings time herald the harsh
body:
It's happened again. Another season, another Manchester United crisis. No longer does the end of daylight savings time herald the harsh winter ahead. Instead, it is the boos that ring around Old Trafford as the United faithful turn their ire on the same owners, the same executives and the same players, well aware it will be a different coach that pays the price.Sunday's 3-0 defeat to AFC Bournemouth was remarkable only for the sheer unremarkability of it. In the 74 years after their first meeting in the 1949 FA Cup third round, Bournemouth won three games against Manchester United. In the last two years they have won three games: all at Old Trafford, all 3-0. Freddie Kruger is treading the boards at the Theatre of Dreams.Although maybe that analogy is not quite apt. After all, the one positive that you could say about a Krugerian nightmare is that it tends to be a one-and-done situation. No such luck if you happen to be a Manchester United supporter. Could any of them now believe that sacking Michael Carrick would fix anything about this club? They've tried the Eddie Howe-esque Premier League mainstay, the relentless winner a la Antonio Conte, the graduate of the Ralf Rangnick pressing academy in the mold of Julian Nagelsmann. Their shortlist only needs an ex-Ajax coach to sweep the quadrants of post-Sir Alex Ferguson ineptitude. Fred Grim to Manchester United? Well, doesn't that sound about right?This is a club suffering under profound mismanagement, the sort that no one individual can marshal on their own. So there's plenty of blame to spread around. Let's start doing so, in reverse order of course. Gotta keep you on the page as long as we can. Build some suspense. Who might be top, you wonder? Well you probably know. But you know most every AAA movie is going to end with the hero triumphant. The joy is in the journey to the inevitable end point.
5. Michael CarrickNow look, the soon to be former Manchester United manager is not without his faults, as Bruno Fernandes so robustly articulated after the 4-1 defeat in Como. There have been some very weird technical decisions here this season and a head coach with a scintilla of authority probably could have got this team to stop taking so many shots from outside the box. And yet did anyone at Manchester United genuinely think they'd unearthed the next great coach when they threw him the salvage our season post-Ruben Amorim job?
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            That Carrick did so much more than that, guiding United to Champions League qualification through a third-placed finish, spoke to his ability to keep things simple. He retained what had worked from his predecessor, tidied up some of the complexities of the formation and rode Bruno Fernandes' player of the season form as far as he could go. It is not his fault that United have not kicked on since. What had the 45 year old achieved in three seasons at Middlesbrough that suggested a coach who would do much more than what most coaches do, get a team to perform at or around its talent level?Maybe when the stars align, when his team has a game a week and a fully fit squad he could achieve something better than the field but it is no more sensible to project out Carrick's future off the spring hot streak than it is to discount his coaching ability because he has struggled to cope with the first confluence of injuries, unfortunate results and player ill-discipline of his tenure.
Old Trafford seemed to have the right sense of it on Sunday. "It's Carrick you know," reverberated around the ground until the minute he was down the tunnel. Then it was both barrels for everyone else.4. The unbearable weight of being Manchester UnitedNo one associated with Manchester United should apologize for having exacting standards. A well-run version of this club would make every decision based on improving their title-winning prospects either in the short or medium term. There should be no need to take the long way to the Premier League summit.Having said all that, goodness it does not take much to send this club into a doom spiral of nostalgia and despair. When Lisandro Martinez served notice on Jason Wilcox and the hierarchy United had performed pretty well in defeat away to Atletico Madrid, a result that few in the Champions League field could credibly bemoan. Their form had wobbled but only a dodgy Erling Haaland goal had taken Manchester City past them and the last two Premier League results had been disappointing but not disastrous draws.
In short things were not going well but the difficulties were explicable. Up to the loss at the Metropolitano at least one of United's major problems was they had scored fewer goals than their expected goals (xG) for and conceded more than the xG value of their opponents shots. Their actual goal difference was minus-one, their expected goal difference was a shade under plus four. There's some heavy lifting being done in there by thrashing Ipswich Town and Sabah but the aggregate of a good team probably does contain a couple of thrashings as well as games where you play even against seemingly inferior teams like Fulham.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            In short, just as United weren't as good as last season's rise to third place -- the defense started wobbling quite dramatically into the spring -- they aren't really as bad as 16th in the table, a point clear of the relegation zone might have you believe. A clear-eyed assessment both of the relative talent of United and the rest of the league would say that this is a good team vulnerable to a wobble. Just stay the course, keep calm in the dressing room and block out the noise.But, of course... this is Manchester United we're talking about.3. The INEOS sporting hierarchySir Jim Ratcliffe certainly talked a good game when he finally got his hands on the sporting infrastructure at Old Trafford in February 2024, his $1.6 billion investment for around a quarter of the club affording him INEOS Group control of football operations at United. No longer would this be a club in hock to the first team head coach, the Ferguson way of thinking to be replaced by a brain trust that included the sporting director, "probably the recruitment guys" and, for reasons, the chief executive and Ratcliffe himself. "In modern football, you need to decide what's your path and stick to your path," the new minority owner insisted.
In the two and a half years since Manchester United's path has led them to: openly canvass the market for a replacement for manager Erik ten Hag, trigger an extension clause in his contract when they couldn't find anyone better, spend over $400 million outfitting the Dutchman with new players, sack him within four months, hire a coach in Ruben Amorim who had talked himself out of better jobs thanks to his insistence on playing a 3-4-3, finish 15th, sack Amorim just as their analytical profile was on an upswing because he had fallen out with his employers, bring in Carrick temporarily and then permanently, spend almost all their budget on midfielders, get dragged in public by Martinez.That's just the condensed lowlights. It's fair to say that you don't hear much any more about Project 150, the ambitious vision to mark a century and a half of the club with a 21st top flight title. Perhaps by 2028 sporting director Wilcox will have got round to fixing the defense having blown so much of the 2025 summer budget on attack before then spending nearly $200 million on a midfield that needed upgrades but got Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba while the left back spot was left untouched.It would say everything about the cataclysmic mismanagement at a senior level if Wilcox -- like so many at the club a man with little top level experience of the role he has been thrust into -- gets the man said to be his preferred choice to succeed Carrick, Eddie Howe.
The same Eddie Howe who spent a hugely successful two years with Dan Ashworth at Newcastle United. The same Dan Ashworth who Manchester United spent £4.1 million on the poaching of and, five months later, firing of. The same Manchester United who in INEOS' period running the show rank ninth in the Premier League for points, 10th for expected goal difference. Still, at least they sacked staff and cut costs. Who ever could have imagined that as a fix for a business' problems?2. The playersSpeaking after Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, Harry Maguire pulled no punches. "At the moment it's nowhere near good enough and something needs to change," he said. He's not wrong. And yet the only constants at this club sit second and first in our rankings. Cast your mind back to the 4-0 thrashing at the hands of Brentford in August 2022, Erik ten Hag's second game in charge and oh, what, half a dozen crises ago. The starting back four for Manchester United on that Saturday evening in west London? Diego Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw. The starting back four in draws against Fulham and Everton more than four years later? Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw.There are players at this club who have seen off half a dozen permanent managers. Some might not have lasted that long but in their time they have been frozen out or put up for sale. Few have paid the price for inconsistency. Why would you respect the authority of the head coach if you have spent three or four years in the Old Trafford dressing room and seen so many cycle through without any apparent accountability for the playing staff. It seems notable that Cristiano Ronaldo's bombing out by Ten Hag was followed by one of the most impressive runs of results in the last half decade. Players discovered their actions had consequences and started playing like that.
Now, they talk like they are bulletproof. Imagine Martin Odegaard used a post-match interview to mouth off about Mikel Arteta's tactics. Would he ever play for Arsenal again? That's a question Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang can answer. When a player did not perform for Pep Guardiola's Manchester City, he was swiftly sold. Meanwhile United's squad is preserved in aspic. Their defense moves like it is.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            These are not players who lack for talent. United's first choice attack rivals any bar Manchester City and Liverpool. Their midfield needs careful construction to mitigate for its lack of pace but it has quality. When the mood takes them Maguire, Martinez and Shaw are perfectly solid defenders. As the graphic above suggests, this is a team that can have moments of extreme competence. That is how United got to third a few months ago. Were they helped by the coach's tactics or the hierarchy's recruitment? Not really but that does not make these expensive, well-remunerated players innocent bystanders, unable to arrest the decline. 1. The GlazersMore than two decades after Malcolm Glazer loaded debt onto Manchester United to fund his purchase of the club, what has been accomplished beyond a steady degradation of this behemoth of English culture. Being owned by the Glazers, who have not put any money into the club since the takeover, is estimated to have cost the club at least $1.5 billion, much of it spent on servicing debt from the initial takeover. It should be noted that 15 major trophies have been won in the time the Glazers have owned the club but 10 of them came in the period where Ferguson's sheer magnetism held the club together.
There is an argument to be made that United's commercial income skyrocketed under current ownership and certainly this was a club that was among the first to realize that every region could have its own bespoke set of sponsors, that there was always another billboard or patch on the jersey to splash with a logo. Those brands were not, however, flocking to United because of anything the Glazers had done. United were the dominant force in English football at just the right moment to benefit from the Premier League moving from national to global obsession.Far from custodians, the Glazers are the most deleterious of landlords. An extractive force, they provide minimal service and value while taking their management fees, dividends, repayments and then the riches Ratcliffe paid for a slice of the pie. All of their money could have gone into retaining United's preeminence in the English game or at least staving off the impact of their indifference. As if to make the metaphor particularly on the nose, on their watch Old Trafford has decayed such that the cost of renovation, an estimated $1.6 billion, might just make a case for the planned new stadium that no supporter seems to want.A club that even in fallow years ranks among the top 10 revenue generators in football has found itself on a cost-cutting drive for which Ratcliffe is the face both because the Glazers' debt acts as a competitive drag and because ownership showed no interest nor aptitude in improving the on-field product. If the players represent a culture that is accountability-lite then it is ownership that enables it. When we start this piece by warning that nothing will change post-Carrick it is because we have seen enough to know that nothing changes until those who tolerate this degradation of Manchester United are no longer in a position of power.

Bucky Irving, Josh Jacobs and Jordan Mason climb the Week 8 Fantasy projections, while J.K. Dobbins faces a declining outlook
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026

    8:17 pm ET

            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In Week 7, we had more players come back from injury than leave injured. We are hoping for more of the same in Week 8. We are expecting Lamar Jackson back against the Bills and view him as a must-start quarterback once again. Elsewhere, there is less certainty. Ladd McConkey, Emeka Egbuka, and DJ Moore could all be back this week at receiver, though they are still questionable as of Monday evening. If all three return, we would start Moore and Egbuka, while viewing McConkey as a low-end WR3. There's less promise at the running back position. It is possible we get Breece Hall and Kyle Monangai back, but that would just create a committee when we already have a workhorse. Most likely, we would have Hall ranked as a low-end RB2 and Braelon Allen as a high-end flex, but Allen has been so good he may hold onto a lot of the early down work. In Chicago, Swift would fall significantly if Monangai returns, partially because of the competition, but also because of the Seahawks' incredible defense.Prominent players, we had projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 8 as of Monday evening: Aaron Jones, Jaylen Waddle, Jaylin NoelAt the bottom of this article are my Week 8 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information. Risers Trevor Lawrence, QB, Jaguars
Last week, Lawrence was on bye, and I don't generally include those guys, but he is QB3 in the early projections, which is much higher than he ranks this season, so I figured it was worth mentioning. His Jaguars have an implied total of 27.5, which is one of the higher marks on the slate, and the Colts defense shouldn't scare anyone. The only way this goes wrong is if they score all their points on the ground. So far this season, 77.8% of their offensive touchdowns have come through the air, so that shouldn't be too big a concern.
Geno Smith, QB, Jets
Smith gets a revenge game against the Raiders. The revenge game portion is not what we are so excited about, even if it is fun to talk about. What is exciting is Smith's collection of weapons after the emergence of Omar Cooper Jr. This could be a legitimately good pass offense. In Week 8, they get a Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most Fantasy points to QBs this season. Each of the last five QBs they have faced has scored at least 21 Fantasy points. Smith is the top streaming option in Week 8.Bucky Irving, RB, Buccaneers
We didn't see the increase in targets I was expecting last week because Tampa Bay completely dismantled the Panthers and Baker Mayfield only threw 11 passes, two of which went to Irving. That only underscores how game-script-independent Irving is. He is running exceptionally well and could have 20 touches on a weekly basis. He's a top 12 running back moving forward and a top 8 back in Week 8.Josh Jacobs, RB, Packers
Jacobs' shake-the-rust-off game was buoyed by better-than-expected usage in the passing game. The rushing efficiency was bad, but that could change in Week 8 as the Packers face the worst run defense in the NFL on a short week. The Panthers have been gashed all season, including last week by all three of Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, and Sean Tucker. I would expect 16 to 20 touches per game from Jacobs and perhaps 16 to 20 Fantasy points in Week 8.
Jordan Mason, RB, Vikings
Aaron Jones' aggravated his knee injury on Sunday and Mason could be a bell cow for the Vikings in a great matchup against Detroit this week. I am not sure he gets enough work in the passing game to rank as a top 12 back like Jones did, but Mason is certainly a start in Week 8. Expect somewhere around 20 touches and 13 fantasy points, depending on how many times Mason gets into the end zone.Tre Tucker, WR, Raiders
Tucker had his second huge game in a row as defenses continue to try to find some way to handle Brock Bowers. Tucker has 19 targets in his last two games and 32 over his last four. He is still a bit of a boom/bust WR3, but with the state of the position this week, that may sneak you inside the top 24. This Raiders/Jets game has sneaky shootout potential. Tucker is a must-start in leagues where you start three receivers.KC Concepcion, WR, Browns
Concepcion's target share had been good for most of the season. In Week 7, we finally saw him turn those targets into Fantasy points. A big difference was his 10.8 aDOT, which was three yards higher than his season average. Hopefully, Todd Monken ticks with that after the great success the rookie had in Week 7. Concepcion and Denzel Boston are both number three receivers this week, and in full PPR, I would rather start the former.
FallersAaron Rodgers QB, Steelers
Rodgers was one of our favorite streamers last week because he was facing the Saints and had been throwing a ton. Unfortunately, the Saints offense didn't show up and the Steelers were able to win the game on the ground. That should be the plan again this week as the Browns pass defense has been above average while they have been one of the worst teams in terms of yards per carry allowed to running backs. Find someone else if you streamed Rodgers last week, preferably Geno Smith.J.K. Dobbins, RB, Broncos
The return of Jonah Coleman has turned this into a full-blown committee. Dobbins was the lead back early in this game, but Coleman dominated playing time and touches in the second half. That may have been because of the game script, but that is exactly the type of game script we were hoping for for Dobbins. If he's sharing early downs and barely involved on passing downs, he is not someone we really even want to flex, particularly in a bad matchup against the Chiefs.Malik Washington, WR, Dolphins
Washington saw his target share shrink last week with Caleb Douglas back in the mix. That's part of the problem. Another part is that the Dolphins face a stingy Patriots defense in Week 8. A bad matchup with increased target competition hits a WR3 hard, even with three receivers on bye. Washington is outside of the top 30 at receiver and depending on who comes back from injury this week, he may be outside of the top 36 in the rankings. He was always a high-floor, low-ceiling play, and now it appears the floor is low as well.
Tyler Higbee, TE, Rams
I can't make any sense of the Rams' tight end rotation and the best way to view it is as if none of them are starters. Colby Parkinson was struggling to get through last week's game, but still a much more popular target than Higbee. Davis Allen is also involved and scored two touchdowns. And Terrance Ferguson could be back in a couple of weeks. There may be another good Higbee week coming but it is hard to count on against the Chargers. I would rather drop him than start him.Week 8 quarterback projections Week 8 running back projections  Week 8 wide receiver projections  Week 8 tight end projections

        Week 7 wraps up on Monday night in Philadelphia, as the Eagles host the rival Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles are still without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. However, running back Saquon Barkley will make his return to the field this week, as he's officially active.Barkley was listed as questionable with a hamstring injury prior to Monday night's game. Barkley returned to practice this week, working as a limited participant during Thursday and Friday's sessions. He was even a full participant on Saturday. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards and zero touchdowns in four games this season, but played under 16% of offensive snaps in half of his appearances. He suffered a stinger at the very beginning of Philly's Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans, and then pulled his hamstring in the first quarter of the Eagles' Week 4 meeting with the Los Angeles Rams. It's been a rough season for the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year, but now that he's nearing a return, Barkley could be ready to take off.Eagles with and without Saquon Barkley this seasonWith BarkleyWithout BarkleyW-L2-20-2Rushing yards per game109.028.5Yards per rush4.21.8Barkley averaged 5.1 yards per rush on 36 rushes this season, while all other Eagles running backs averaged 2.8 yards per rush on 71 attempts. The Eagles ran the ball with Dameon Pierce just 12 times last week against the Carolina Panthers, netting 35 yards and a touchdown.
With all of the injuries, this Eagles offense has struggled this season. They have averaged fewer than 4.0 yards per play over three straight games within a season for the first time since 1999, and have been out-gained by 108.3 total yards per game this season, which ranks worst in the NFL. With that said, the Cowboys could be a get-right game for this squad if Barkley is back. body:
As the Raiders stumble to 3-4 ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, contenders like the Bears and Bills could pursue the star pass rusher to fuel a playoff push
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Las Vegas Raiders have now gone from 3-0 to 3-4. Just a few weeks ago, they were one of the biggest surprises in the NFL, but have since become a losing team that could be making a quarterback change in the near future. Their swift fall from undefeated to losing record could also change how the organization approaches the upcoming trade deadline. It's again time to debate if the Raiders should trade one of their best players, pass rusher Maxx Crosby. We listed him as a player we would like to see get a change of scenery recently, but it remains to be seen if that's in the cards for Vegas. Crosby was traded to the Baltimore Ravens this offseason for two first-round picks. However, the Ravens backed out of the deal when their staff discovered something worrisome during the in-person physical. ESPN's Adam Schefter mentioned recently that it's unknown if Crosby is pushing for a trade behind closed doors, as he was several months ago. Maybe he viewed the canceled trade with Baltimore as divine intervention signaling he was meant to be a Raider for life. Plus, what would Vegas want for him at this point? It's hard to imagine the Raiders fetching two first-round picks again. With that said, senior NFL writer Pete Prisco argued on CBS Sports HQ this past Sunday that the Raiders should trade Crosby and pick up further draft capital to help in the rebuild they are currently in. Those picks, he said, could be used when Fernando Mendoza eventually takes over.
Maybe Crosby only fetches a first-round pick and a fourth-round pick this time around. Is that good enough for Raiders' GM John Spytek to consider? Crosby is one of the best defensive ends in the NFL. Not only does he get after quarterbacks, having recorded four double-digit sack seasons, but no player has recorded more tackles for loss (136) since Crosby entered the league in 2019. His 25 pressures this season rank second in the NFL behind Greg Rousseau.The Raiders trading Crosby prior to the Nov. 10 deadline would be a bit surprising. If they decided to part ways with a star talent, where could Crosby land? Let's take a look at four potential landing spots. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago BearsThe Chicago Bears were deemed the prime regression candidate in the NFC this year following their magical 11-6 campaign in 2025, when they registered an NFL-record seven wins when trailing in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, including playoffs. But with Caleb Williams under center, who says Chicago has to regress? The Bears do have some tough games coming up against the Seattle Seahawks, Detroit Lions, Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills, but through seven weeks, Chicago is sitting pretty at 5-2.
The Bears' pass rush could be improved. It's pretty unbelievable that cornerback Kyler Gordon has played in just two games this season and is tied with Austin Booker for the team lead with four sacks. Chicago also just saw Montez Sweat get suspended two games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing drugs policy, while Dayo Odeyingbo is currently out with a quadriceps injury. The Bears make sense for Crosby if he's moved. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Detroit LionsThere's another team in the NFC North where Crosby could potentially be a fit, and it's the team he grew up rooting for. The Lions are actually tied for the league lead in sacks this season with 21, but the defense still ranks dead last with 391.0 yards allowed per game. I think it's possible Kelvin Sheppard's unit is on the upswing. Not only did they hold Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers to 17 points on Sunday, but Brian Branch is back in the lineup, and Kerby Joseph could be back soon as well. Imagine if the Lions added Crosby to rush the passer opposite of Aidan Hutchinson? Maybe this is more wishful thinking, but the Lions could become the new favorite in the NFC North if they made this deal. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas CowboysSome people, like myself, thought the Dallas Cowboys defense was going to be much improved in 2026. That has not been the case, as they rank third-worst in total yards allowed per game (382.5) entering their Monday night matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys took a swing on former Pittsburgh Steelers corner Joey Porter Jr., and they could make another deal in acquiring a pass rusher to help boost a unit that is tied for fourth-worst in sacks with eight. This would be an aggressive and controversial swing of the bat from Jerry Jones. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buffalo BillsLet's get a little wild. The Bills made it clear they were "Super Bowl or bust" when they fired Sean McDermott last year, but this Jim Leonhard defense needs some work. Buffalo has won four games this year, and all four victories came in matchups where the Bills allowed 30+ points! The rest of the NFL was 8-42 through Week 6 in games where defenses allowed at least 30 points. The Bills ranked first in points per drive (3.13) and last in points per drive allowed (2.76) after Week 6. 
Imagine pairing Greg Rousseau and Deone Walker with a talent like Crosby, and what that could do for this defense and team at large.

        Allow me to reintroduce the Super Bowl halftime performer ... his name is Jay-Z. Using a snippet from one of his most iconic songs, "Public Service Announcement," the rapper was announced as the Super Bowl LXI halftime performer. This is the first time he will take the Super Bowl halftime stage.Here is a look at the announcement:
Roc Nation, co-founded by Jay-Z, partnered with the NFL in 2019 to produce the halftime show. HOV has a major influence in choosing the performer, and this year he went with himself.While the 89-time Grammy nominee has not announced any special guests yet, there are already numerous names that come to mind for potential additions, including superstar singer Beyoncé, previous halftime performers Rihanna and Eminem.
The Super Bowl, concluding the 2026 season, will be played at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California on February 14, 2027.The halftime show has been headlined by some of the biggest artists of all time and has delivered wild, iconic moments throughout the Super Bowl's 60-year history.Last year, Bad Bunny headlined, taking the stage at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. Lady Gaga joined him on stage to perform her hit, "Die With A Smile," marking her third Super Bowl appearance and first as a halftime show guest. 
Other past headliners include Kendrick Lamar, Rihanna, Usher and Beyoncé. For artists who play the Super Bowl halftime show, the audience is exponentially bigger than any they have ever encountered. It was not always like that, however.So what were the shows like before they became must-see television? Do you remember that killer halftime show featuring the Rockettes, Chubby Checker and 88 grand pianos in 1988? Do you remember the captivating "Be Bop Bamboozled" at the Orange Bowl in 1989? No -- no, you do not. Ditto Carol Channing (twice) or any of those four contrived Up With People performances in the late '70s and early '80s.Before Michael Jackson, the Super Bowl halftime show was an endless wasteland of college marching bands and flag-spinning tributes -- from salutes to Hollywood (twice), to Motown, to the Big Band Era, to the Caribbean, to Duke Ellington. Aspiring sports bettors who want to focus more on daily fantasy sports have a handful of options, with one of those outfits is PrizePicks. We'll look at the latest PrizePicks promo code the platform is offering for NFL Week 7 and what users who sign up can expect to receive.PrizePicks promo code for October 2026PrizePicks is offering $50 to users who make a $5 play or more in a contest on one of the leading DFS apps. Here's how those interested can get the offer.PrizePicks promo codeNone requiredPrizePicks Fantasy bonus offerPlay $5, Get $50PrizePicks Fantasy legal states45 states and Washington D.C.PrizePicks Fantasy deposit methodsPayPal, Venmo, Bank Account, Apple Pay, Credit/Debit CardTerms and conditionsMust be of legal age in a state where PrizePicks operatesPromo code last verifiedOctober 26, 2026There are other DFS platforms outside of PrizePicks offering promotions for new users. Here's a look at the offers from Underdog and Dabble. DFS AppBonus offerPromo codePrizePicksPlay $5, Get $50 None requiredUnderdogPlay $10, Get $50 in Bonus EntriesCBSDabblePlay $10, get $20 in bonus cashCBSDABPrizePicks is offering a promotion most similar to Dabble, as both offer bonus entries. Underdog offers $50 in bonus entries after a new user plays $10.PrizePicks Fantasy minimum age, terms and conditionsMost users must be at least 18 years old to sign up for PrizePicks. Users in Alabama and Colorado must be at least 19 years old, while users in Arizona, Iowa, Louisiana and Massachusetts must be at least 21 years old.How to sign up for PrizePicks promo codeGo to PrizePicks.com and click on the "Claim Your $50 Now". Make sure your location services are enabled so the platform can verify your eligibility to play.Enter your information to create an account and make a deposit of at least $10. Make sure there is a promo code being applied. The code might vary depending on how you've attempted to sign up.Submit your first lineup in a contest for at least $5.PrizePicks will deposit $50 in promo funds to your account.How to play on PrizePicks Fantasy appThere are three different contests users can enter on PrizePicks. The most common type of contest, Pick 'Em, is available in 19 states plus Washington D.C. In this format, users select two to six player statistics to make predictions on, guessing if the player will go higher or lower than the number for that statistic by selecting "More" or "Less." Just click the Board button at the bottom of the PrizePicks app to get started. At the top of the Board section, you can choose which sport you want and begin building an entry. For example, after choosing NBA, I was presented with potential player picks and various categories to choose from, like points, rebounds and assists. On this day, I chose rebounds and added:Ausar Thompson more than six reboundsKarl-Anthony Towns less than 13 reboundsMyles Turner more than 6.5 reboundsA pop-up to Finalize Lineup appeared which allowed me to complete my entry and choose what kind of entry I wanted to play. Users can choose whether to submit their entry as a Flex or Power Play. In a Flex Play, users can get picks incorrect and still receive a payout. With the example entry above, two correct picks was worth 1x, which is just your full entry fee amount returned. Three correct picks out of three in this Flex Play returned 2.25x. So a $10 entry would have returned $22.50. Users must select at least three picks to be eligible for Flex Play.In a Power Play, users must get all picks correct to get paid out. Three out of three picks for the entry above returned 5x ($50 payout on $10 entry). Here are the payouts details on PrizePicks:Number of selectionsPower Play payoutFlex Play payout6 picks37.5x6/6 - 25x5/6 - 2x4/6 - 0.4x5 picks20x5/5 - 10x4/5 - 2x3/5 - 0.4 x4 picks10x4/4 - 5x3/4 - 1.5x3 picks5x3/3 - 2.25x2/3 - 1.25x2 picks3xN/APick 'Em Arena, which is available to users in 17 states, follows the same payout structure as Pick 'Em. For users in Colorado, each entry in Pick 'Em Arena must contain at least three picks. The entry follows the same format as Pick 'Em, but user entries are automatically submitted to a group depending on the time of submission, user's skill level and number of picks made. Based on how you do in the group, you can win even more. If multiple players tie for first place in a group, the prize is split unless there's a winning Flex lineup in the group. Here's how picks are scored in a group setting.Type of projectionPointsDemon1.05Standard1Goblin0.95Discounted0.95DNP0.5Push (tied)0.5Reboot0Lose (incorrect pick)0 A "demon" pick is a projection square which is red, meaning that prediction is harder to win. A "goblin" pick is a projection square which is green, meaning that prediction is easier to win. You must pick "More" on both demon and goblin projections.For example, one Goblin pick for Spurs guard Stephon Castle in the NBA was more than 17 points, even though he was averaging 24 points per game at the time of writing. Meanwhile, Knicks guard Jalen Brunson had available Demon picks of more than 29.5, 32.5 and 34.5 points, despite averaging just 26 points per game at the time of writing. Streak is available in 10 states. This is a free-to-play option on PrizePicks and helps users get additional rewards as they build wins. The idea is a user must make one prediction on any player. If that pick is correct, the user's streak is extended to the next day to make one more pick. As the user keeps getting picks correct, he or she unlocks more rewards. According to PrizePicks, the cash prize in Streak could be up to $1 million depending on how many wins you string together.PrizePicks says it pays out users within 30 minutes of a contest settling. Most lineups are generally settled once the official score is finalized after a game ends. PrizePicks says users who have to wait longer than 30 minutes for a payout for all completed projections in a lineup should reach out to the live support team.PrizePicks Fantasy promos and bonuses for existing usersPrizePicks offers regular bonuses for existing users. Referral bonuses can be earned up to 10 times in a 30-day period. Users can access referral codes from the PrizePicks app or website in the "Get $" tab or the "Invite Friends" link. Once the referred user signs up using the referral code and makes a deposit, the existing users get a referral bonus.Reboots occur when a player unexpectedly exits a game. If this occurs, entries are modified in the same way they would be for a player not participating. This means that leg of the entry is voided, with the other legs still available. In NFL, college basketball, NBA and WNBA contests, entries are eligible for a reboot when a user selects "More" on a player's projection, the player exits the game in the first half and does not return for the second half. In MLB contests, reboots occur when a user selects "More" on a player's projection and that player leaves after making two or fewer plate appearances.Original entryReboot entry6 pick Flex5 pick Flex5 pick Flex4 pick Flex4 pick Flex3 pick Flex4 pick Power3 pick Power3 pick Flex2 pick Power3 pick Power2 pick Power2 pickRefundedTaco Tuesday is another regular promotion at PrizePicks. Every Tuesday, several player projections will be discounted by 15-25%. These player headshots will be replaced by a taco, so users know which projections are discounted. Users can vote in the PrizePicks Discord (members only) or PrizePicks X account on which players they want to get a discounted projection for that Tuesday.Flex Friday is another regular promotion on the platform. In the Promos tab on the app or website, users can "opt in" to Flex Friday protected plays by noon ET. Users then create a flex play lineup and check "Flex Friday Protected Play." If the lineup wins, users get paid out. If the lineup loses, users get promotional funds up to the previously decided limit. If a lineup partially wins, users can get a bit of both offers.For example, let's say your promo limit is $20 and you submit a 6-pick Flex lineup, winning four of your picks. You will be credited $8 for those wins, and your $12 loss will be deposited back into your account as promo funds. This minimizes risk, although you cannot withdraw promotional funds from your account. Promo limits vary depending on the user, and you cannot enter Flex Friday using promo funds. Flex Friday cannot be combined with other discounts or offers.PrizePicks Fantasy app review: user experienceThe PrizePicks app is straightforward to use, featuring a menu at the bottom to help users track their picks, use promotions and access help. Selecting players is also straightforward, with the "demon" and "goblin" tiles clearly indicated for users wishing to add those specific selections. There's a search function as well for users to find players they want to make predictions on. There's a drop-down menu available as well, which is more functional for the website rather than the mobile app. This menu is located on the right side on the website, while it is on the left side in the app.App storeNumber of reviewsAverage rating (as of October 26, 2026)Apple510k4.7Android76k4.4There are extensive resources for responsible gaming at PrizePicks, which can be found using the drop-down menu in the app or on the website. Users can set alerts and limits while also taking timeouts or self-excluding. A unique feature here is age-based deposit limits, which are automatically applied to users under 21. 18-year-olds have a $1,500 monthly deposit limit, 19-year-olds have a $3,000 monthly limit and 20-year-olds have a $5,000 monthly limit.Here's a look at the sports PrizePicks offers contests for:FootballBasketballBaseballHockeySoccerOlympicsTennisRacingEsportsGolfCricketJai AlaiLacrosseCombatPrizePicks also offers contests for special competitions, such as the Fourth of July hot dog eating contest and NBA All-Star events.PrizePicks Fantasy customer supportUsers experiencing issues can email support@prizepicks.com, but the most unique thing about this platform is the 24/7 live chat offering. Users can access this function on the app or website and chat with a support member at any time for any questions. For quick inquiries about funds, contests or eligibility, this function can be more useful than sending an email. Live chat features are not commonly found on DFS platforms and are more likely to be seen for sportsbook platforms. If you are not satisfied with an outcome provided by customer support, you can email dispute@prizepicks.com to escalate your issue.PrizePicks Fantasy banking methodsDeposits can be made to a PrizePicks account from PayPal, Venmo, a bank account, credit/debit card or Apple Pay. However, there are some restrictions depending on the user's state.Visa credit cards and Discover credit/debit cards can only be used for deposits. The same applies to Apple Pay. Mastercard credit cards are available in every state except South Carolina. PayPay and Venmo are not available in New Hampshire, Maine, Missouri, Colorado and Delaware. Withdrawing funds is a bit of a challenge. Users must request a withdrawal using the drop-down menu on the app or website. Funds can be withdrawn to a bank, PayPal, Venmo or a debit card previously used to deposit funds into PrizePicks, outside of Discover debit cards. Users must withdraw at least $10 for the action to be processed. Only one withdrawal is permitted in a 24-hour window but most customers are eligible for instant withdrawal. Some customers might be under a review process, so withdrawals may take 6-12 hours to process.A wrinkle with PrizePicks is the one-time playthrough requirement before withdrawing funds. For example, if you deposit $20 into a PrizePicks account, you must play through $20 worth of lineups to be able to withdraw money. This applies to any amount of deposited funds, so users should be wary about how much they are investing if they are unsure about using the platform or playing daily fantasy sports. While most platforms do have this restriction, it's usually only for bonus funds issued by the company.PrizePicks Fantasy review: final grades and ratingsHere's a breakdown of PrizePicks and the biggest takeaways from the platform.Promo code and welcome bonus: 9/10Promos and bonuses for existing users: 10/10User experience: 8/10DFS scoring settings: 6/10Customer support: 8/10Banking methods: 4/10PrizePicks has a solid welcome bonus for those interested in getting into DFS without making too big of an investment. PrizePicks also has great payouts compared to some other platforms, and has regular rewards for existing users like Taco Tuesday and Flex Friday. These promotions give users a great opportunity twice a week for better chances at payouts. The user experience is similar to most DFS platforms, with a few minor adjustments between the app and website.While the DFS scoring settings on PrizePicks don't vary from other platforms by category, the specific point totals are not easily found on the app or website. This can cause some confusion for users, especially those who are new to DFS and wondering how the scoring system works. title: Jalen Williams leg injury: Top-20 NBA star stretchered off court after gruesome fall - CBS Sports
description: Williams was stretchered off the court on Sunday night -- and he's not the only major injury concern for OKC
body:
Williams was stretchered off the court on Sunday night -- and he's not the only major injury concern for OKC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams will need to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle, OKC general manager Sam Presti said Monday. An exact return timeline won't be known until after surgery, Presti said, but ESPN reported that it could be a season-ending injury. Presti disclosed Monday that Thunder guard Cason Wallace will also need surgery. Wallace hurt his shoulder against the Clippers on Sunday and will undergo a procedure to repair a torn labrum. Wallace, too, could be out for the season, per ESPN, but the Thunder had no official timeline on his potential return."Tough night last night. There's no way to paint that differently," Presti told reporters.Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher late in the fourth quarter of a 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night after suffering the severe lower leg injury. With just over a minute to play, Williams drove to the basket and tried to go up for a dunk. He was sandwiched in mid-air by Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr., which caused him to lose his balance. When he landed, his left leg got trapped underneath the weight of his entire body and the lower part of it appeared to break in the wrong direction. 
The Thunder training staff immediately covered his leg with towels as his teammates looked on in distress. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander pulled his own jersey up over his face as Williams' leg was placed into an air cast and he was loaded onto a stretcher. "I just feel bad for him. Nothing more than that," Gilgeous-Alexander said on the court after the win. Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said the team had no immediate update on Williams' status. 
"We're not doing great," Daigneault said. "That's tough on the guys." 
Williams gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was wheeled off the court.Williams was coming off season derailed by injuriesWilliams, 25, emerged as a true star in 2025, when he made his first All-Star appearance and earned a spot on the All-NBA Third Team and the All-Defensive Second Team before helping Gilgeous-Alexander lead the Thunder to their first title since moving to Oklahoma City. Williams averaged 23.6 points in the 2025 Finals and had a playoff-career-high 40 points to lead the Thunder to a Game 5 win that gave them a 3-2 series lead over the Pacers (OKC won in seven games). He played through a wrist injury during the 2025 playoffs, however, and underwent surgery last summer to fix the problem, which kept him sidelined for the first 19 games of last season. Less than two months into his return, he strained his right hamstring and was sidelined for multiple weeks. He came back, played two games, then tweaked his hamstring again and missed another six weeks. Williams returned shortly before the playoffs last season, but suffered a left hamstring strain in Game 2 of the Thunder's first-round series with the Phoenix Suns. He sat out the rest of that series and missed the entire second round before coming back for the Western Conference Finals against the Spurs. After a stellar Game 1, he tweaked his left hamstring again in Game 2 and only played 10 more minutes the rest of the series. 
When the Thunder lost Game 7 to the Spurs, which ended their repeat quest, he was forced to watch from the bench in street clothes. 
        
            
                What Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace injuries mean for the Thunder and why a trade isn't so simple
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Williams and Wallace injuries a major blow to OKC's title chancesThe Thunder made some moves around the margins this offseason -- most notably, trading Lu Dort to the Atlanta Hawks -- but brought back their entire core and hoped to make another run at the title in a top-heavy Western Conference. Vegas oddsmakers installed them as the preseason favorite to win the title, and they started the season with a convincing win over the Spurs. Though he was off to a somewhat slow start, Williams was averaging 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and one steal to begin the season, and was second on the team in scoring behind Gilgeous-Alexander. CBS Sports ranked Williams as the 20th-best player in the NBA in the annual Top 100 player rankings. 
Sunday's win over the Clippers moved the Thunder to 3-0, and even without Dort, they have the depth to withstand Williams' absence -- at least in the regular season. They won 64 games last season largely without Williams. But it will be tougher to withstand Williams' absence with Wallace joining him on the bench.A fourth-year guard, Wallace had worked his way into the OKC starting lineup. He made All-Defense Second Team last season while averaging 8.6 points per game. His emergence was one of the reasons why the Thunder felt comfortable trading away a veteran like Dort. Wallace had started in all three games this season before the injury.Williams' injury draws comparisons to Hayward'sThe gruesome nature of Williams' injury and the reactions it elicited from teammates reminded fans of Gordon Hayward's injury nine years ago.
Hayward, like Williams, dislocated his left ankle and fractured his left tibia on opening night of the 2017-18 season in his debut with the Celtics. He missed the remainder of that season and was never the same player. Hayward appeared in 318 more games over six seasons before retiring at 33 years old.

title: Robert Griffin III would '100% be interested' in Baylor head coaching job - CBS Sports
description: Could Baylor's former Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback be a serious candidate to replace the fired Dave Aranda?
body:
Could Baylor's former Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback be a serious candidate to replace the fired Dave Aranda?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Despite having no coaching experience at any level, former Baylor Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Robert Griffin III would be interested in the Bears' vacancy following Sunday's firing of coach Dave Aranda.Griffin, a college football analyst and Texas native, wants to see his former program nationally relevant again at the highest level."If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor," Griffin said Monday on the Dan Patrick Show. "So yeah, I would 100% be interested. I talked with the athletic director, who is a guy in Doug McNamee that knows what it looks like to win at Baylor, know how you have to win at Baylor and recruit to Baylor to make those things happen."
Griffin set several single-season program records at Baylor in 2011 after throwing for 4,293 yards and 37  touchdowns, to go along with 699 yards rushing and 10 scores. He later earned NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors before injuries derailed a promising career.Since Griffin helped the Bears capture their 10th win in the Alamo Bowl to end this tenure, Baylor has hit 11 or more wins in a single season three times -- including a 12-2 finish in 2021 under Aranda as the Big 12 champions. Only one winning season since fueled Baylor's decision to cut ties with Aranda over the weekend after a loss to Kansas.Griffin mentioned UTSA's Jeff Traylor and Boise State's Spencer Danielson as two coaches he would advocate for the job, along with USC's Lincoln Riley. 
 "I know (Riley's) got his experiences at Oklahoma and obviously, what's going on at USC right now," Griffin said.
        
            
                Baylor football coaching search 2026: Candidates, hot board, names to watch from Bears experts
                
                    Daniel Lewis                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Baylor not the only Power Four vacancyPerhaps Griffin stated publicly that he would be interested in Baylor due to the recent development that another Power Four job, NC State, is considering former Wolfpack quarterback and NFL great Philip Rivers for its new head coach.Like Griffin, Rivers is beloved by his former program and enjoyed some of the best seasons in program history during his tenure at NC State in the early 2000s. However, Rivers has coached prep football in Alabama the last six seasons and interviewed in January for the Buffalo Bills' job.
McNamee has been Baylor's new AD for 11 months, and this will mark the first major hire of his tenure. The Bears expect to have a roster capable of competing in the Big 12 next season, including the return of transfer quarterback DJ Lagway in 2027.CBS Sports previously reported the program will likely look for a coach with Texas roots and one who's offensive-minded.
